cond_0001.intro:
The Almada Laboratory at [Company name masked] is investigating how stem cells are activated to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. Their multi-disciplinary team integrates experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this at the molecular, cellular, and organ level across vertebrate species including lizards, mice, and humans. They also investigate how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, with the goal of translating basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity. The lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and an R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
For this position, we are seeking a postdoctoral fellow to engage in a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to facilitate this translational work.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Serve as a research trainee for the purpose of enhancing and developing research competencies. Participates in planning, designing, and conducting highly technical and complex research projects under the direction of a supervisor. He/she may or may not work independently. Analyzes and evaluates research data utilizing computers and provides interpretations requiring significant knowledge of a specialized area of research. Searches literature, utilizing all available resources including electronic, regarding new methodology and designs experiments accordingly. Contributes to the development of research documentation for publication and/or prepares technical reports, papers, and/or records. Candidate will work on research projects in a highly interdisciplinary environment. Will work with senior research associates, technicians, PhD, and master's students on projects related to stem cell biology and aging.
Performs other related duties as assigned or requested. The university reserves the right to add or change duties at any time.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Ph.D. Or equivalent doctorate within previous five years
0-1 Year experience
Ph.D. In any area of molecular, cellular, stem cell biology, or computational biology
Strong background in molecular and cellular biology
Directly related education in any area of stem cell biology with advanced knowledge of equipment, procedures and analysis methods
Preferred Requirements
Experience with at least one of the following: mouse genetics, fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), proteomics, or bioinformatic analysis
Publications in peer-reviewed journals in the same or related field

The Almada Laboratory investigates how stem cells are activated to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. The lab uses experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this at the molecular, cellular, and organ level across vertebrate species including lizards, mice, and humans. The lab also examines how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, with the aim of translating basic science findings into therapies relevant to human health and longevity. The lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and an R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
This position focuses on a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. There is an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to support this translational work.
cond_0133.responsibilities:
Serve as a research trainee for the purpose of enhancing and developing research competencies.
Participate in planning, designing, and conducting highly technical and complex research projects under the direction of a supervisor. May or may not work independently.
Analyze and evaluate research data using computers and provide interpretations requiring significant knowledge of a specialized area of research.
Search literature using all available resources including electronic sources regarding new methodology, and design experiments accordingly.
Contribute to the development of research documentation for publication and/or prepare technical reports, papers, and/or records.
Work on research projects in a highly interdisciplinary environment.
Coordinate with senior research associates, technicians, PhD, and master's students on projects related to stem cell biology and aging.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested. The university reserves the right to add or change duties at any time.
cond_0133.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Ph.D. Or equivalent doctorate within previous five years
0-1 Year experience
Ph.D. In any area of molecular, cellular, stem cell biology, or computational biology
Strong background in molecular and cellular biology
Directly related education in any area of stem cell biology with advanced knowledge of equipment, procedures, and analysis methods
Preferred Requirements
Experience with at least one of the following: mouse genetics, fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), proteomics, or bioinformatic analysis
Publications in peer-reviewed journals in the same or related field

The Keck School of Medicine (KSOM) at [Company name masked] is currently seeking a Postdoctoral Scholar to join the Laboratory of Dr. Albert E. Almada in the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery; Department of Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine (SCRM); and Leonard Davis School of Gerontology.
The Almada Laboratory is investigating one of the greatest mysteries in muscle regenerative biology—how stem cells are turned on (activated) to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. Their multi-disciplinary team integrates state-of-the-art experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this biological phenomenon at the molecular, cellular, and organ level in various vertebrate species, ranging the evolutionary continuum from lizards, to mice, and humans. Importantly, they investigate how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, hoping to translate their basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity. The Almada lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and a recent R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
For this position, we are seeking a postdoctoral fellow to engage in a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to facilitate this translational work. cond_0221.intro:
The Keck School of Medicine (KSOM) at [Company name masked] is currently seeking a Postdoctoral Scholar to join the Laboratory of Dr. Albert E. Almada in the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery; Department of Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine (SCRM); and Leonard Davis School of Gerontology.
The Almada Laboratory is investigating one of the greatest mysteries in muscle regenerative biology—how stem cells are turned on (activated) to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. Their multi-disciplinary team integrates state-of-the-art experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this biological phenomenon at the molecular, cellular, and organ level in various vertebrate species, ranging the evolutionary continuum from lizards, to mice, and humans. Importantly, they investigate how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, hoping to translate their basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity. The Almada lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and a recent R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
For this position, we are seeking a postdoctoral fellow to engage in a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to facilitate this translational work. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with stem cell and molecular biology research.
cond_0221.responsibilities:
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
Serve as a research trainee for the purpose of enhancing and developing research competencies. Participates in planning, designing, and conducting highly technical and complex research projects under the direction of a supervisor. He/she may or may not work independently. Analyzes and evaluates research data utilizing computers and provides interpretations requiring significant knowledge of a specialized area of research. Searches literature, utilizing all available resources including electronic, regarding new methodology and designs experiments accordingly. Contributes to the development of research documentation for publication and/or prepares technical reports, papers, and/or records. Candidate will work on research projects in a highly interdisciplinary environment. Will work with senior research associates, technicians, PhD, and master's students on projects related to stem cell biology and aging.
Performs other related duties as assigned or requested. The university reserves the right to add or change duties at any time.
cond_0221.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Ph.D. Or equivalent doctorate within previous five years
Ph.D. In any area of molecular, cellular, stem cell biology, or computational biology
Strong background in molecular and cellular biology
Directly related education in any area of stem cell biology with advanced knowledge of equipment, procedures and analysis methods
0-1 Year experience
Preferred Requirements:
Experience with at least one of the following: mouse genetics, fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), proteomics, or bioinformatic analysis
Publications in peer-reviewed journals in the same or related field

The Keck School of Medicine (KSOM) at [Company name masked] is currently seeking a Postdoctoral Scholar to join the Laboratory of Dr. Albert E. Almada in the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery; Department of Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine (SCRM); and Leonard Davis School of Gerontology.
The Almada Laboratory is investigating one of the greatest mysteries in muscle regenerative biology—how stem cells are turned on (activated) to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. Their multi-disciplinary team integrates state-of-the-art experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this biological phenomenon at the molecular, cellular, and organ level in various vertebrate species, ranging the evolutionary continuum from lizards, to mice, and humans. Importantly, they investigate how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, hoping to translate their basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity. The Almada lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and a recent R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
For this position, we are seeking a postdoctoral fellow to engage in a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to facilitate this translational work. People typically become stronger in this kind of research over time as they build hands-on experience and learn from the work itself.

Candidate will work on research projects in a highly interdisciplinary environment. cond_0240.intro:
The Keck School of Medicine (KSOM) at [Company name masked] is looking for a Postdoctoral Scholar to join the Laboratory of Dr. Albert E. Almada in the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery; Department of Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine (SCRM); and Leonard Davis School of Gerontology.
The Almada Laboratory is investigating one of the greatest mysteries in muscle regenerative biology—how stem cells are turned on (activated) to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. The lab's multi-disciplinary team integrates experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this at the molecular, cellular, and organ level across vertebrate species, from lizards to mice to humans. They also investigate how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, with the goal of translating basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity. The lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and a recent R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
For this position, we are looking for a postdoctoral fellow to work on a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to support this translational work.
cond_0240.responsibilities:
Serve as a research trainee to build and develop research competencies. Actively participate in planning, designing, and conducting highly technical and complex research projects under the direction of a supervisor. Analyze and evaluate research data using computers and provide interpretations requiring significant knowledge of a specialized area of research. Search literature using all available resources, including electronic, on new methodology and design experiments accordingly. Contribute to the development of research documentation for publication and prepare technical reports, papers, and records. Work on research projects in a highly interdisciplinary environment, staying in regular contact with senior research associates, technicians, PhD, and master's students on projects related to stem cell biology and aging.
Performs other related duties as assigned or requested. The university reserves the right to add or change duties at any time.
cond_0240.requirements:

Ph.D. Or equivalent doctorate within the previous five years
0-1 Year experience
Ph.D. In any area of molecular, cellular, stem cell biology, or computational biology
Strong background in molecular and cellular biology
Direct education in any area of stem cell biology with advanced knowledge of equipment, procedures, and analysis methods
Preferred Requirements
Experience with at least one of the following: mouse genetics, fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), proteomics, or bioinformatic analysis

cond_0311.intro:
The Keck School of Medicine (KSOM) at [Company name masked] is currently seeking a Postdoctoral Scholar to join the Laboratory of Dr. Albert E. Almada in the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery; Department of Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine (SCRM); and Leonard Davis School of Gerontology.
The Almada Laboratory is investigating one of the greatest mysteries in muscle regenerative biology—how stem cells are turned on (activated) to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. Their multi-disciplinary team integrates state-of-the-art experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this biological phenomenon at the molecular, cellular, and organ level in various vertebrate species, ranging the evolutionary continuum from lizards, to mice, and humans. Importantly, they investigate how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, hoping to translate their basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity. The Almada lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and a recent R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
For this position, we are seeking a postdoctoral fellow to engage in a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to facilitate this translational work. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with stem cell and molecular biology research.

cond_0395.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Scholar to join the Laboratory of Dr. Albert E. Almada in the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery; Department of Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine (SCRM); and Leonard Davis School of Gerontology at [Company name masked].
The Almada Laboratory is investigating one of the greatest mysteries in muscle regenerative biology—how stem cells are turned on (activated) to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. Their multi-disciplinary team integrates state-of-the-art experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this biological phenomenon at the molecular, cellular, and organ level in various vertebrate species, ranging the evolutionary continuum from lizards, to mice, and humans. Importantly, they investigate how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, hoping to translate their basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity. The Almada lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and a recent R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
For this position, we are seeking a postdoctoral fellow to lead a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to facilitate this translational work.

cond_0452.intro:
The Keck School of Medicine (KSOM) at [Company name masked] is currently seeking a talented and self-motivated Postdoctoral Scholar to join the Laboratory of Dr. Albert E. Almada in the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery; Department of Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine (SCRM); and Leonard Davis School of Gerontology.
The Almada Laboratory is investigating one of the greatest mysteries in muscle regenerative biology—how stem cells are turned on (activated) to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. Their multi-disciplinary team integrates state-of-the-art experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this biological phenomenon at the molecular, cellular, and organ level in various vertebrate species, ranging the evolutionary continuum from lizards, to mice, and humans. Importantly, they investigate how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, hoping to translate their basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity. The Almada lab is currently supported by two Junior Faculty awards from the Baxter Foundation, Glenn Foundation/American Federation of Aging Research (AFAR), and a recent R01 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS).
For this position, we are seeking a postdoctoral fellow to engage in a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to facilitate this translational work.

The lab is investigating how stem cells are activated to rebuild functional muscle tissue after traumatic injury. Our multi-disciplinary team works together using experimental and bioinformatic approaches to study this at the molecular, cellular, and organ level across vertebrate species including lizards, mice, and humans. Together, we explore how stem cell dysfunction contributes to aging and muscular dystrophy, with the shared goal of translating basic science discoveries into therapies that benefit human health and longevity.
For this position, we are looking for a postdoctoral fellow to collaborate on a project involving stem cell dysfunction in muscular dystrophy using mouse and human model systems. We have an ongoing collaboration with [Company name masked] to obtain muscle samples from DMD patients to support this translational work.
cond_0513.responsibilities:
Serve as a research trainee to develop and strengthen research competencies in collaboration with the team. Work alongside supervisors and colleagues in planning, designing, and conducting highly technical and complex research projects. Contribute to data analysis and interpretation using computational tools, drawing on specialized knowledge of the research area. Coordinate with team members to search literature and identify new methodology, and help design experiments accordingly. Share in the development of research documentation for publication and assist in preparing technical reports, papers, and records. Collaborate with senior research associates, technicians, PhD, and master's students on projects related to stem cell biology and aging.
Performs other related duties as assigned or requested. The university reserves the right to add or change duties at any time.
cond_0513.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Ph.D. Or equivalent doctorate within previous five years
0-1 Year experience
Directly related education in any area of stem cell biology with advanced knowledge of equipment, procedures, and analysis methods
Strong background in molecular and cellular biology

Experience with at least one of the following: mouse genetics, fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), proteomics, or bioinformatic analysis
